characterization_methods.key_findings: Equiaxed grains with prominent straight annealing-twin lamellae and dotted dark particles; coarse-grained annealed structure.
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal annealed microstructure and grain size of hot-rolled Fe-7Al VIM.
Determine alloy composition of the Fe-7Al VIM ingot.
characterization_methods.technique: chemical composition analysis (including hydrogen by RH-444 Leco Gas analyzer)

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure bulk hardness of hot-rolled Fe-7Al VIM.

characterization_methods.key_findings: UTS 445 ± 5.6 MPa, YS 360 ± 7.5 MPa, total elongation 20 ± 2.1%
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: average of three tests, room temperature
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure room-temperature tensile properties of hot-rolled Fe-7Al VIM.

processing_steps.cooling_medium: poured into 80-mm-diameter split cast iron molds kept inside the vacuum chamber
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 50-kg capacity, 125-kW medium-frequency chamber vacuum induction furnace; alumina-lined crucible approximately 150 mm diameter and 300 mm height; soft iron pieces charged at bottom with aluminum pieces on top; power switched on after evacuation to 10^-4 torr.
Hot-forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature.
Preheating of 24-mm-thick sections of forged billets.
Hot rolled with 1-mm reduction in thickness per pass; samples reheated after every six rolling passes under similar conditions as preheating; final hot-rolled plate thickness 12 mm.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Hardness: average of five measurements; tensile: average of three tests.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with prominent straight annealing-twin lamellae

structures.overall_structure: Annealed microstructure with coarse grain size; single-phase disordered Fe-Al solid solution; equiaxed grains with prominent straight annealing-twin lamellae and dotted dark particles (interpreted as residual porosity/second-phase particles).

unmapped_findings: Fe-7Al VIM ingots were sound and completely free from microcracks as well as hydrogen gas porosity (b0018).
Fe-7Al VIM exhibited excellent hot workability; the alloy could also be cold rolled to thin sheets and foils (b0041).
Measured composition of Fe-7Al VIM (Table I): Al 7.02, Si 0.12, Mn 0.052, S 0.0028, C 0.015, O 0.0035, H 0.0020, N <0.001 wt.% (b0035/b0036/figure_unlabelled_001).

Room-temperature tensile ductility of Fe-7Al VIM was comparable to the AIMFC-produced alloy and superior to the AIM-produced alloy; poor AIM ductility was attributed to hydrogen embrittlement and oxide/sulfide inclusions (b0042).
General context: density of iron-aluminum alloys was noted as 6.7 g/cm^3 (b0015); this is a general alloy-system value, not a sample-specific measurement.
